brief:
Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, is attempting to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu through a subdued approach, according to Al-Monitor. Eisenkot, who typically dresses in black and speaks halting English, reflects the military culture that defined his career. In interviews, he tends to respond with bullet-point lists rather than elaborate rhetoric.

The effort represents a potential challenge to Netanyahu's political dominance, though details of Eisenkot's formal campaign structure and timing remain limited in available reporting.
dek: Gadi Eisenkot, the man who could unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, almost always dresses in black, speaks halting English and tends to respond in interviews with bullet-point lists, a reflection of the military culture that shaped him.
title: Eisenkot pursues quiet campaign to challenge Netanyahu's leadership
